assign.outcome:
**The Playwright post is live** — [/blog/ai/playwright/](/blog/ai/playwright/), *"Playwright: a browser you can write to"*, 1,809 words, an 8 minute read, five sections and six exhibits.

![the post at 1920: the measure on the left, the first exhibit floated beside the head](post-1920.jpg)

**The takeaway, in the post's own words:** Playwright is a program that opens a real web browser you cannot see, and then does exactly what a script tells it — which is why one tool ends up testing a website, reading data off one, photographing one, and giving an AI agent hands on the web.

**What is in it** — every section leads with its exhibit:
1. What it is, and the four lines that are the whole idea.
2. What people use it for — testing first, then scraping, visual regression, PDFs, scheduled monitoring, CI.
3. The three ways Claude Code drives a browser: the accessibility snapshot (`@playwright/mcp`), pixels (computer use), and scripts the model writes itself (this repo's [`ui-test` habit](/framework/ai/2026-08-19/ui-test-skill/) and [vision runner](/framework/ext/DesignTool/vision/)).
4. What it did tonight — sixty sites, fifty-one loaded, nine stopped by bot walls, twenty-five embeddable; four widths each; [/websites/](/websites/) and [/layouts/](/layouts/).
5. The honest limits — bot detection, hiQ (won on the CFAA, still paid $500,000 on contract), auto-waiting is not a flakiness cure, the cross-origin CSSOM, and the "42% faster" stat that has no source, filed *fringe*.

**Exhibits** (all from [the ten demos](/blog/ai/playwright/demo/readme.md), none re-shot): `01` four widths · `03` click-and-type · `06` images blocked · `09` a real `ariaSnapshot()` beside the same page as a picture · `10` MDN headless · plus the `page.route` block carrying [the font-loader trap](/framework/ai/2026-09-08/font-fallback/) found earlier tonight.

**Also landed:** the entry in [`posts.js`](/blog/posts.js); `card.png` (1200x628, cropped from demo 01 with Playwright itself, PNG so the shell gets real `og:image:width`); the four generated files re-stamped by `meta.mjs`; and two now-true sentences on [the research front](/imagine/research/) (five topics, four ancient and one on browser automation).

**Proof:** zero console errors, zero page errors, zero failed requests at 400, 1280, 1920 and 3440; no sideways scroll at any width; 6 figures, 5 pictures, 0 broken; the card is first on [/blog/](/blog/). One defect found and fixed by measuring rather than eyeballing — the prose code block was 88 characters wide where the measure column fits 69, clipping its first comment at every width above 400.

**Left, with reasons:** `public/blog/readme.md` needs one Watch out line — *`image:` must be a PNG; `png_size()` reads an IHDR, so a .jpg card unfurls with no width or height* — but the readme is outside this task's write fence, so the reason is written into the `posts.js` entry instead. And `/imagine/research/`'s `question:` ("What do we actually know about ancient technology…") is now also half-true with a fifth topic; the brief fenced this task to exactly two sentences there, so it is flagged, not edited.
